Disorders of Protein and Lipid Glycosylation (ICIMD category 18)

The umbrella union of inherited disorders in which the lesion is in the attachment, remodeling, or removal of a glycan on a protein or a lipid. Glycans are added to most secreted and membrane proteins and to a large class of lipids; a defect anywhere in that machinery — precursor supply, transfer to the acceptor, Golgi maturation, or the cytosolic clearance of released glycans — hypoglycosylates many client molecules at once, which is why the resulting diseases are characteristically multisystem. This grouping points down to five nested sub-groupings drawn on the branch of the glycosylation machinery that fails: protein N-glycosylation, protein O-glycosylation (including the glycosaminoglycan chains built on an O-xylose), GPI-anchor (lipid) glycosylation, precursor-supply and ER-quality-control lesions that hit several branches at once, and cytosolic deglycosylation.

38 disease entries belong to this grouping through nested groupings. They appear in the coverage table below as nested members, are evaluated against the membership criteria like direct members, and count toward coverage.

Why this grouping

Grouped on the shared mechanism family — a lesion in glycoconjugate metabolism, with hypoglycosylation (or, for the deglycosylation arm, failure to clear a released glycan) as the common intermediate lesion — and on an established nosological convention: category 18 of the International Classification of Inherited Metabolic Disorders (ICIMD; Ferreira et al. 2021, PMID:33340416), whose own subdivision into N-linked, O-linked, lipid, and multiple-pathway glycosylation disorders is what the nested sub-groupings mirror. This grouping points down to nested sub-groupings rather than listing member diseases flatly, following the pattern of Inborn_Errors_of_Immunity over the IUIS tables. It adds no direct disease members of its own. Each child keeps its own, narrower NECESSARY criterion; this parent's criterion is the disjunction of theirs, so any disease that satisfies its own sub-grouping necessarily satisfies this one. Why this exists rather than being folded into the existing Congenital_Disorders_of_Glycosylation grouping. That grouping is deliberately scoped to protein N-glycosylation and its precursor and trafficking supply lines — a boundary its own rationale states and defends — while binding MONDO:0015286 (congenital disorder of glycosylation), which is the broader concept covering O-linked, GPI-anchor, and glycosphingolipid defects as well. A grouping cannot both be deliberately narrower than a concept and exactMatch it. Creating the umbrella resolves that: the exactMatch to MONDO:0015286 moves here, and the N-glycan grouping is downgraded to skos:narrowMatch, which still counts as curated for MONDO coverage. Naming. ICIMD titles category 18 "Congenital disorders of glycosylation", but that name is already taken in kb/groupings/ by the N-glycan-scoped child and grouping names are foreign-key targets, so renaming it would break existing references and history records. This grouping therefore takes a descriptive name; "ICIMD category 18" is carried in display_name so the correspondence is not lost. Boundary — two exclusions worth recording, because both are things a reader would expect to find here. Glycogen storage diseases are out: glycogen is a storage homopolysaccharide, not a glycoconjugate, and ICIMD places disorders of glycogen metabolism outside the glycan-metabolism categories explicitly. The mucopolysaccharidoses are also out: they are lysosomal catabolism of glycosaminoglycans, already held by Mucopolysaccharidoses beneath Lysosomal_Storage_Disorders, and ICIMD places glycosaminoglycan *synthesis* under O-linked protein glycosylation rather than placing GAG degradation in category 18. Both are glycobiology in the loose sense; neither is a defect of glycan attachment to a protein or lipid.

MONDO alignment & provenance

skos:exactMatch MONDO:0015286 · congenital disorder of glycosylation

MONDO:0015286 is the broad congenital-disorder-of-glycosylation class, spanning N-linked, O-linked, GPI-anchor, and glycosphingolipid defects. That is this grouping's concept, not the narrower N-glycan concept of the nested Congenital_Disorders_of_Glycosylation child, which now carries skos:narrowMatch against the same term. MONDO descendants without DisMech entries are curation gaps rather than a reason to downgrade the predicate.

MONDO consistency: inconsistent Re-derived 2026-09-18 over all 38 transitively held members: 24 are hierarchical descendants of MONDO:0015286 and 14 are not. Recorded as INCONSISTENT because that is what was measured; the mapping predicate is deliberately left at skos:exactMatch pending a decision, and this note is the evidence for that decision rather than a pre-emption of it. Method, reproducible without a local MONDO build: each member's own MONDO term is resolved to its ancestor set via the OLS hierarchicalAncestors endpoint and MONDO:0015286 looked up in it — one bounded upward walk per member (13-38 terms) instead of one unbounded downward expansion of the class. The OAK ols:mondo adapter raises NotImplementedError for both directions, but the REST endpoint underneath answers ancestors. The 14 divide into two kinds, and only one is a defect. (1) Genuine scope difference: MONDO scopes congenital disorder of glycosylation narrower than ICIMD category 18 does. The two deglycosylation members sit under MONDO:0031376 congenital disorder of deglycosylation, a *sibling* of MONDO:0015286 beneath MONDO:0019052 inborn errors of metabolism, and five of the six GPI-anchor members are likewise outside the class. ICIMD puts both inside category 18; MONDO does not. (2) Classification by clinical presentation rather than mechanism: Dystroglycanopathy sits under muscular dystrophy, Autosomal Recessive Cutis Laxa Type 2A under cutis laxa and hereditary skin disorder (verified against its direct parents, which carry no CDG term), the SLC10A7 and EXTL3 entries under skeletal system disorder, the PIG-gene entries under the epilepsies, and VPS51-CDG under pontocerebellar hypoplasia. These are candidate MONDO term requests, not membership errors. What this means for the predicate: the umbrella's concept properly *contains* the MONDO class rather than equalling it, which is skos:broadMatch and not skos:exactMatch. The reason it has not simply been flipped is that the change is not free — per CLAUDE.md a broadMatch does not count as curated for MONDO coverage, and scripts/grouping_mondo_gaps.py derives descendant gaps only from an exactMatch, so flipping it here after the N-glycan child was downgraded to narrowMatch would leave MONDO:0015286 with no exactMatch anywhere in the family and silently end gap derivation for the whole CDG branch. Semantics and tooling disagree; that is a design call for the decision register, not a predicate to change twice in two days.

Membership criteria

NECESSARY  (member ⇒ criteria)
A member is an inherited disorder whose proximal lesion is in the biosynthesis, transfer, remodeling, or removal of a glycan attached to a protein or a lipid — including the nucleotide-sugar and dolichol precursor supply feeding those steps, the Golgi machinery that matures the glycan, and the cytosolic enzymes that clear a released glycan. Disorders of glycogen metabolism and of lysosomal glycosaminoglycan catabolism are excluded.
  • OR The disjunction of the five nested sub-groupings' own NECESSARY criteria. Stated as a union rather than as a single broader process term because no one GO class subsumes protein glycosylation, GPI-anchor (lipid) glycosylation, and protein deglycosylation; a member satisfies this parent through whichever branch its own sub-grouping already requires.
    • HAS BIOLOGICAL PROCESS protein N-linked glycosylation GO:0006487
      Involves protein N-linked glycosylation (assembly/transfer) — the Congenital_Disorders_of_Glycosylation branch.
    • HAS BIOLOGICAL PROCESS N-glycan processing GO:0006491
      Involves N-glycan processing (Golgi maturation) — the Congenital_Disorders_of_Glycosylation branch.
    • HAS BIOLOGICAL PROCESS GPI anchor biosynthetic process GO:0006506
      Involves GPI anchor biosynthesis — the Disorders_of_GPI_Anchor_Biosynthesis branch, ICIMD's lipid-glycosylation subdivision.
    • HAS BIOLOGICAL PROCESS protein glycosylation GO:0009101
      Involves glycoprotein biosynthesis without the lesion being specific to a named branch — the Other_Multiple_Glycosylation_Pathway_Disorders branch, whose members are there precisely because their lesion spans several. Ontology closure makes this subsume the two N-linked and the O-linked operands, which are kept so a member's own branch stays readable off the criterion that matched it.
    • HAS BIOLOGICAL PROCESS protein O-linked glycosylation GO:0006493
      Involves protein O-linked glycosylation — the Disorders_of_O-linked_Protein_Glycosylation branch (O-mannose, O-glucose/O-fucose, and the O-xylose glycosaminoglycan linker). Also satisfied by Other_Multiple_Glycosylation_Pathway_Disorders members whose branch-non-specific lesion reaches O-glycans.
    • HAS BIOLOGICAL PROCESS glycosaminoglycan biosynthetic process GO:0006024
      Involves glycosaminoglycan biosynthesis — the GAG-*synthesis* arm that ICIMD places under O-linked protein glycosylation. Note this is biosynthesis, not the lysosomal catabolism of the mucopolysaccharidoses.
    • HAS BIOLOGICAL PROCESS protein folding in endoplasmic reticulum GO:0034975
      Involves ER protein folding — carried because Other_Multiple_Glycosylation_Pathway_Disorders requires it for UGGT1, whose lesion is re-glucosylation-based quality control of N-glycans.
    • HAS BIOLOGICAL PROCESS proteoglycan biosynthetic process GO:0030166
      Involves proteoglycan biosynthesis — carried because Disorders_of_O-linked_Protein_Glycosylation requires it for the two members that annotate only the proteoglycan-product classes (GO:0015012, GO:0050650) rather than the glycosaminoglycan class. Without it this disjunction was not in fact the union of its children's criteria, which is what the logic description above claims.
    • HAS BIOLOGICAL PROCESS protein deglycosylation GO:0006517
      Involves protein deglycosylation — the Congenital_Disorders_of_Deglycosylation branch.
    • HAS BIOLOGICAL PROCESS oligosaccharide catabolic process GO:0009313
      Involves oligosaccharide catabolism — the Congenital_Disorders_of_Deglycosylation branch (free-oligosaccharide trimming).
SUFFICIENT  (criteria ⇒ member)
An entry assigned to ICIMD category 18 — congenital disorders of glycosylation, or any of its N-linked, O-linked, lipid, multiple-pathway, or other-glycan-metabolism subdivisions — via classifications.icimd_category belongs in this grouping.
  • OR A discovery criterion, not an audit of the listed members: it is stated SUFFICIENT so that entries carrying an ICIMD category-18 value but not yet reached by any nested sub-grouping surface as candidate additions. Those currently outstanding are named in notes. It is deliberately not NECESSARY — most listed members carry no icimd_category value at all, and a NECESSARY reading would report that curation gap as a membership contradiction.
    • HAS CLASSIFICATION
      ICIMD category 18 at the category level.
    • HAS CLASSIFICATION
      ICIMD 18, N-linked protein glycosylation.
    • HAS CLASSIFICATION
      ICIMD 18, O-linked protein glycosylation (incl. GAG synthesis).
    • HAS CLASSIFICATION
      ICIMD 18, lipid glycosylation (incl. GPI biosynthesis).
    • HAS CLASSIFICATION
      ICIMD 18, disorders affecting multiple glycosylation pathways (dolichol metabolism, Golgi transport and homeostasis, sialic acid metabolism).
    • HAS CLASSIFICATION
      ICIMD 18, other disorders of glycan metabolism.

ALG1-congenital disorder of glycosylation DISEASE
Differentiating mechanism
ALG1 is the beta-1,4-mannosyltransferase that adds the first mannose to the cytosolic-face dolichol-linked GlcNAc2 precursor; deficiency (CDG-Ik) blocks LLO assembly at its earliest mannosylation step, upstream of the ALG3/ALG9/ALG12 elongation reactions.

CCDC115-CDG DISEASE
Differentiating mechanism
Golgi V-ATPase assembly, so the proximal lesion is Golgi luminal pH rather than any glycosyltransferase. It sits with the trafficking-and-homeostasis arm of this grouping (COG1, COG7, VPS51) and, like them, produces a combined N- and O-glycosylation defect; the distinguishing clinical feature is hepatopathy with abnormal copper metabolism.

CHIME_syndrome DISEASE
Differentiating mechanism
CHIME syndrome (colobomas, heart defects, ichthyosiform dermatosis, mental retardation, ear anomalies) is caused by biallelic PIGL variants. PIGL encodes the de-N-acetylase that removes the acetyl group from N-acetylglucosaminyl-phosphatidylinositol, the second step of GPI anchor synthesis — an early assembly-step defect, distinct from the remodeling defects of Mabry syndrome.

Mabry Syndrome DISEASE
Differentiating mechanism
Mabry syndrome (hyperphosphatasia with mental retardation syndrome, HPMRS) is caused by biallelic defects in the mannosyltransferase/ethanolamine-phosphate-transferase steps of GPI assembly (PIGV, PIGO) and in the post-attachment fatty-acid remodeling steps (PGAP2, PGAP3). In both the assembly-step (PIGV/PIGO) and remodeling-step (PGAP2/PGAP3) defects the GPI-anchored alkaline phosphatase is shed into serum instead of being retained at the cell surface, producing the characteristic hyperphosphatasia that distinguishes this arm of the group.
Mabry syndrome

PMM2-Congenital Disorder of Glycosylation DISEASE
Differentiating mechanism
Phosphomannomutase 2 interconverts mannose-6-phosphate and mannose-1-phosphate, the step that feeds GDP-mannose into the whole lipid-linked oligosaccharide assembly line. Its deficiency (CDG-Ia) is therefore upstream of every mannosyltransferase defect in this grouping: ALG1, ALG3, ALG9 and ALG12 each lose one step, while PMM2 loss starves all of them of donor. It sits alongside MPI and PGM1 as a precursor-supply defect rather than an assembly defect, and MPI is its instructive counterpart — the adjacent step in the same supply line, but treatable with oral mannose where PMM2-CDG is not. PMM2-CDG is also the reference case for the group clinically. It is the commonest CDG by a wide margin and the one whose phenotype the others are described against, and it is where the group's genetic architecture is clearest: complete loss of activity is not compatible with survival, so patients are hypomorph compound heterozygotes and per-allele residual activity sets severity.
PMM2-congenital disorder of glycosylation

Peters plus syndrome DISEASE
Differentiating mechanism
O-glucosylation of thrombospondin type-1 repeats. B3GLCT extends the O-fucose on a correctly folded TSR with glucose, so the client set is the TSR-containing ADAMTS and ADAMTSL secreted proteins rather than a membrane glycoprotein, and the disease is an anterior-segment dysgenesis with skeletal features.

DHRSX-Congenital Disorder of Glycosylation DISEASE
Differentiating mechanism
DHRSX-CDG (CDG1DD) is a type I CDG upstream of LLO assembly: the defect is in dolichol synthesis itself rather than in transferring sugars onto it. DHRSX performs the first and third steps of the three-step conversion of polyprenol to dolichol, with SRD5A3 catalysing only the second, so its loss raises the polyprenol-to-dolichol ratio and starves every downstream dolichol-dependent step at once. It is also the only member with pseudoautosomal-recessive inheritance, since DHRSX lies in PAR1 of the X and Y chromosomes.
congenital disorder of glycosylation, type 1DD

Seizures-scoliosis-macrocephaly syndrome DISEASE
Differentiating mechanism
Heparan sulfate chain polymerization. Biallelic hypomorphic EXT2 shortens the chain rather than initiating it, and is a distinct disease from the heterozygous EXT2 loss that causes hereditary multiple exostoses — the same gene, a different dose and a different phenotype.

Autosomal Recessive Cutis Laxa Type 2A DISEASE
Differentiating mechanism
ATP6V0A2, the Golgi V-ATPase a2 subunit. The lesion is Golgi luminal acidification, not a transferase or a nucleotide-sugar pool, and it disables N- and O-linked glycosylation together — which is what places it here rather than in a branch-specific sibling. The distinguishing consequence is defective elastic-fibre assembly, giving cutis laxa beside the neuronal migration defect.
ATP6V0A2-related cutis laxa

Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria DISEASE
Differentiating mechanism
Paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria is the ACQUIRED member: a somatic PIGA mutation in a hematopoietic stem cell abolishes the committed first step of GPI anchor synthesis (transfer of GlcNAc to phosphatidylinositol). The resulting loss of GPI-anchored complement regulators CD55 and CD59 on the clonal red cells causes complement-mediated intravascular hemolysis. Unlike the germline members it is X-linked-somatic and clonal, not inherited, and its phenotype is hematologic rather than a developmental encephalopathy.

Developmental And Epileptic Encephalopathy 38 DISEASE
Differentiating mechanism
DEE38 is the ARV1 arm of inherited GPI deficiency. ARV1 is not a PIG/PGAP biosynthetic enzyme but a facilitating component of the GPI-GnT complex that initiates GPI-anchor assembly (it associates with PIGQ and promotes recruitment of the phosphatidylinositol substrate), so ARV1 loss reduces GPI-anchor synthesis at its very first, committed step. Patient neutrophils and fibroblasts show reduced surface GPI-anchored proteins, placing DEE38 among the inherited GPI-deficiency disorders; the phenotype is an autosomal-recessive developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with progressive cerebral and cerebellar atrophy, without the hyperphosphatasia of the Mabry/HPMRS arm. Its membership rests on the NECESSARY GO:0006506 criterion rather than on MONDO ancestry — MONDO does not yet classify MONDO:0014868 under disorder of GPI anchor biosynthesis.

Developmental And Epileptic Encephalopathy 77 DISEASE
Differentiating mechanism
DEE77 (PIGQ-CDG, MCAHS4, GPIBD19) is the PIGQ arm of inherited GPI deficiency. PIGQ is a component of the GPI-N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase complex that performs the first committed step of the pathway — transfer of GlcNAc from UDP-GlcNAc onto phosphatidylinositol on the cytoplasmic face of the ER — so the lesion sits alongside PIGA, PIGC, PIGH, PIGP and PIGY rather than at the mannosyltransferase or remodelling steps. Patient granulocytes, leukocytes and fibroblasts show reduced surface GPI-anchored proteins, restored by wild-type PIGQ cDNA. The phenotype is a severe autosomal recessive developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with multiple congenital anomalies, high childhood mortality (median survival 5.5 years across the 13 published patients), and a consistent craniofacial gestalt. It differs from the other first-step members curated here in one respect worth flagging: elevated serum alkaline phosphatase is reported in 62% of PIGQ patients, which the pathway-position account of hyperphosphatasia — a Mabry/HPMRS feature arising from mannose-bearing incomplete anchors — does not predict for a block this early. That tension is recorded as a knowledge gap on the disease entry rather than resolved here.
developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 77

Multiple Congenital Anomalies-Hypotonia-Seizures Syndrome DISEASE
Differentiating mechanism
MCAHS is the severe developmental-and-epileptic-encephalopathy arm of germline inherited GPI deficiency, an umbrella over three subtypes defined by the affected GPI-pathway gene: MCAHS1 (PIGN, ethanolamine-phosphate transfer), MCAHS2 (PIGA, the committed first GlcNAc-transfer step; X-linked and mechanistically distinct from the somatic-PIGA clone of PNH), and MCAHS3 (PIGT, GPI transamidase attachment). Unlike the Mabry/HPMRS arm, MCAHS does not show persistent hyperphosphatasia (serum alkaline phosphatase is normal, or low in PIGT/MCAHS3), and the clinical picture is dominated by multiple congenital anomalies and early-onset drug-resistant epileptic encephalopathy rather than the bone-enzyme abnormality.

Differentiating mechanism
SLC10A7, a Golgi calcium-handling transporter. Like the ATP6V0A2 member the proximal lesion is a Golgi luminal condition rather than a glycosylation enzyme, but the perturbed variable is calcium rather than pH, and the client range extends to glycosaminoglycan synthesis as well as N- and O-glycans — hence a skeletal dysplasia with amelogenesis imperfecta.

Congenital Disorders of Deglycosylation GROUPING
Differentiating mechanism
ICIMD 18, other disorders of glycan metabolism — the direction-reversed arm. Where the other three children fail to attach a glycan, these fail to remove and clear one: cytosolic peptide:N-glycanase (NGLY1) releasing the N-glycan from a retrotranslocated misfolded glycoprotein, and cytosolic alpha-mannosidase (MAN2C1) trimming the free oligosaccharide that release generates. The conforming module is cytosolic_deglycosylation, not congenital_disorder_of_glycosylation.

Congenital Disorders of Glycosylation GROUPING
Differentiating mechanism
ICIMD 18, N-linked protein glycosylation. Defects in the assembly of the dolichol-linked oligosaccharide precursor, its transfer to nascent protein, or its Golgi remodeling, together with the nucleotide-sugar and dolichol supply lines feeding them (ALG1/3/9/12, DPM2, MPDU1, DOLK, PMM2, MPI, PGM1, MGAT2, SLC35A2, COG1, COG7, VPS51, DHRSX), plus ER glucosidase-I trimming (MOGS), terminal antenna galactosylation (B4GALT1), and Golgi V-ATPase assembly (CCDC115). The diagnostic readout is the serum transferrin glycoform profile, type I versus type II.

Disorders of GPI Anchor Biosynthesis GROUPING
Differentiating mechanism
ICIMD 18, lipid glycosylation. Defects in assembly, transfer, or post-attachment remodeling of the glycosylphosphatidylinositol anchor, so the affected clients are the GPI-anchored surface proteins rather than the N-glycoproteins (PIGA, PIGL, PIGP, PIGV, PIGO, PGAP2, PGAP3). Hyperphosphatasia from unanchored alkaline phosphatase, and — for the somatic PIGA case, paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria — complement-mediated hemolysis from lost CD55/CD59, are the distinguishing readouts.

DisMech only
Disorders of O-linked Protein Glycosylation GROUPING
Differentiating mechanism
ICIMD 18, O-linked protein glycosylation, including glycosaminoglycan synthesis. Defects in a glycan attached to a serine or threonine hydroxyl rather than an asparagine amide, divided by first sugar: O-mannose on alpha-dystroglycan (the dystroglycanopathy gene series), O-glucose on thrombospondin type-1 repeats (B3GLCT), and the O-xylose linker that starts every glycosaminoglycan chain (B3GAT3, EXTL3, EXT2). Distinguished from the N-glycan child by linkage chemistry and client protein family, and from the multiple-pathway child by the lesion being confined to this branch.
No MONDO identity yes no no MONDO ID listed not evaluated not evaluated not evaluated not evaluated not evaluated not evaluated not evaluated not evaluated not evaluated not evaluated not evaluated not evaluated not evaluated not evaluated not evaluated not evaluated not evaluated
DisMech only
Other Disorders of Multiple Glycosylation Pathways GROUPING
Differentiating mechanism
ICIMD 18, disorders affecting multiple glycosylation pathways. Lesions upstream of, or lateral to, any single branch: UDP-sugar precursor supply serving glycosaminoglycan, glycolipid, and protein glycosylation at once (UGDH, UGP2), and ER re-glucosylation quality control of N-glycoproteins (UGGT1), and Golgi luminal conditions that disable several branches at once — pH via the V-ATPase a2 subunit (ATP6V0A2) and calcium handling (SLC10A7). Distinguished from the N-glycan child by the lesion not being specific to one glycosylation branch.

Raw YAML 
name: Disorders of Protein and Lipid Glycosylation
display_name: Disorders of Protein and Lipid Glycosylation (ICIMD category 18)
creation_date: "2026-09-17T00:00:00Z"
description: >-
  The umbrella union of inherited disorders in which the lesion is in the
  attachment, remodeling, or removal of a glycan on a protein or a lipid. Glycans
  are added to most secreted and membrane proteins and to a large class of lipids;
  a defect anywhere in that machinery — precursor supply, transfer to the acceptor,
  Golgi maturation, or the cytosolic clearance of released glycans — hypoglycosylates
  many client molecules at once, which is why the resulting diseases are
  characteristically multisystem. This grouping points down to five nested
  sub-groupings drawn on the branch of the glycosylation machinery that fails:
  protein N-glycosylation, protein O-glycosylation (including the
  glycosaminoglycan chains built on an O-xylose), GPI-anchor (lipid)
  glycosylation, precursor-supply and ER-quality-control lesions that hit
  several branches at once, and cytosolic deglycosylation.
grouping_basis:
- SHARED_MECHANISM
- CLINICAL_CONVENTION
grouping_rationale: >-
  Grouped on the shared mechanism family — a lesion in glycoconjugate metabolism,
  with hypoglycosylation (or, for the deglycosylation arm, failure to clear a
  released glycan) as the common intermediate lesion — and on an established
  nosological convention: category 18 of the International Classification of
  Inherited Metabolic Disorders (ICIMD; Ferreira et al. 2021, PMID:33340416),
  whose own subdivision into N-linked, O-linked, lipid, and multiple-pathway
  glycosylation disorders is what the nested sub-groupings mirror.

  This grouping points down to nested sub-groupings rather than listing
  member diseases flatly, following the pattern of Inborn_Errors_of_Immunity over
  the IUIS tables. It adds no direct disease members of its own. Each child keeps
  its own, narrower NECESSARY criterion; this parent's criterion is the
  disjunction of theirs, so any disease that satisfies its own sub-grouping
  necessarily satisfies this one.

  Why this exists rather than being folded into the existing
  Congenital_Disorders_of_Glycosylation grouping. That grouping is deliberately
  scoped to protein N-glycosylation and its precursor and trafficking supply
  lines — a boundary its own rationale states and defends — while binding
  MONDO:0015286 (congenital disorder of glycosylation), which is the broader
  concept covering O-linked, GPI-anchor, and glycosphingolipid defects as well.
  A grouping cannot both be deliberately narrower than a concept and exactMatch
  it. Creating the umbrella resolves that: the exactMatch to MONDO:0015286 moves
  here, and the N-glycan grouping is downgraded to skos:narrowMatch, which still
  counts as curated for MONDO coverage.

  Naming. ICIMD titles category 18 "Congenital disorders of glycosylation", but
  that name is already taken in kb/groupings/ by the N-glycan-scoped child and
  grouping names are foreign-key targets, so renaming it would break existing
  references and history records. This grouping therefore takes a descriptive
  name; "ICIMD category 18" is carried in display_name so the correspondence is
  not lost.

  Boundary — two exclusions worth recording, because both are things a reader
  would expect to find here. Glycogen storage diseases are out: glycogen is a
  storage homopolysaccharide, not a glycoconjugate, and ICIMD places disorders of
  glycogen metabolism outside the glycan-metabolism categories explicitly. The
  mucopolysaccharidoses are also out: they are lysosomal catabolism of
  glycosaminoglycans, already held by Mucopolysaccharidoses beneath
  Lysosomal_Storage_Disorders, and ICIMD places glycosaminoglycan *synthesis*
  under O-linked protein glycosylation rather than placing GAG degradation in
  category 18. Both are glycobiology in the loose sense; neither is a defect of
  glycan attachment to a protein or lipid.
mappings:
  mondo_mappings:
  - term:
      id: MONDO:0015286
      label: congenital disorder of glycosylation
    mapping_predicate: skos:exactMatch
    mapping_source: MONDO
    mapping_justification: >-
      MONDO:0015286 is the broad congenital-disorder-of-glycosylation class,
      spanning N-linked, O-linked, GPI-anchor, and glycosphingolipid defects.
      That is this grouping's concept, not the narrower N-glycan concept of the
      nested Congenital_Disorders_of_Glycosylation child, which now carries
      skos:narrowMatch against the same term. MONDO descendants without DisMech
      entries are curation gaps rather than a reason to downgrade the predicate.
    consistency:
    - reference: MONDO
      consistent: INCONSISTENT
      notes: >-
        Re-derived 2026-09-18 over all 38 transitively held members: 24 are
        hierarchical descendants of MONDO:0015286 and 14 are not. Recorded as
        INCONSISTENT because that is what was measured; the mapping predicate is
        deliberately left at skos:exactMatch pending a decision, and this note is
        the evidence for that decision rather than a pre-emption of it.

        Method, reproducible without a local MONDO build: each member's own MONDO
        term is resolved to its ancestor set via the OLS hierarchicalAncestors
        endpoint and MONDO:0015286 looked up in it — one bounded upward walk per
        member (13-38 terms) instead of one unbounded downward expansion of the
        class. The OAK ols:mondo adapter raises NotImplementedError for both
        directions, but the REST endpoint underneath answers ancestors.

        The 14 divide into two kinds, and only one is a defect. (1) Genuine scope
        difference: MONDO scopes congenital disorder of glycosylation narrower
        than ICIMD category 18 does. The two deglycosylation members sit under
        MONDO:0031376 congenital disorder of deglycosylation, a *sibling* of
        MONDO:0015286 beneath MONDO:0019052 inborn errors of metabolism, and five
        of the six GPI-anchor members are likewise outside the class. ICIMD puts
        both inside category 18; MONDO does not. (2) Classification by clinical
        presentation rather than mechanism: Dystroglycanopathy sits under
        muscular dystrophy, Autosomal Recessive Cutis Laxa Type 2A under cutis
        laxa and hereditary skin disorder (verified against its direct parents,
        which carry no CDG term), the SLC10A7 and EXTL3 entries under skeletal
        system disorder, the PIG-gene entries under the epilepsies, and
        VPS51-CDG under pontocerebellar hypoplasia. These are candidate MONDO
        term requests, not membership errors.

        What this means for the predicate: the umbrella's concept properly
        *contains* the MONDO class rather than equalling it, which is
        skos:broadMatch and not skos:exactMatch. The reason it has not simply
        been flipped is that the change is not free — per CLAUDE.md a broadMatch
        does not count as curated for MONDO coverage, and
        scripts/grouping_mondo_gaps.py derives descendant gaps only from an
        exactMatch, so flipping it here after the N-glycan child was downgraded
        to narrowMatch would leave MONDO:0015286 with no exactMatch anywhere in
        the family and silently end gap derivation for the whole CDG branch.
        Semantics and tooling disagree; that is a design call for the decision
        register, not a predicate to change twice in two days.
membership_criteria:
- description: >-
    A member is an inherited disorder whose proximal lesion is in the
    biosynthesis, transfer, remodeling, or removal of a glycan attached to a
    protein or a lipid — including the nucleotide-sugar and dolichol precursor
    supply feeding those steps, the Golgi machinery that matures the glycan, and
    the cytosolic enzymes that clear a released glycan. Disorders of glycogen
    metabolism and of lysosomal glycosaminoglycan catabolism are excluded.
  criteria_semantics: NECESSARY
  logic:
    operator: OR
    description: >-
      The disjunction of the five nested sub-groupings' own NECESSARY criteria.
      Stated as a union rather than as a single broader process term because no
      one GO class subsumes protein glycosylation, GPI-anchor (lipid)
      glycosylation, and protein deglycosylation; a member satisfies this parent
      through whichever branch its own sub-grouping already requires.
    operands:
    - criterion_predicate: HAS_BIOLOGICAL_PROCESS
      description: >-
        Involves protein N-linked glycosylation (assembly/transfer) — the
        Congenital_Disorders_of_Glycosylation branch.
      biological_processes:
      - preferred_term: protein N-linked glycosylation
        term:
          id: GO:0006487
          label: protein N-linked glycosylation
    - criterion_predicate: HAS_BIOLOGICAL_PROCESS
      description: >-
        Involves N-glycan processing (Golgi maturation) — the
        Congenital_Disorders_of_Glycosylation branch.
      biological_processes:
      - preferred_term: N-glycan processing
        term:
          id: GO:0006491
          label: N-glycan processing
    - criterion_predicate: HAS_BIOLOGICAL_PROCESS
      description: >-
        Involves GPI anchor biosynthesis — the
        Disorders_of_GPI_Anchor_Biosynthesis branch, ICIMD's lipid-glycosylation
        subdivision.
      biological_processes:
      - preferred_term: GPI anchor biosynthetic process
        term:
          id: GO:0006506
          label: GPI anchor biosynthetic process
    - criterion_predicate: HAS_BIOLOGICAL_PROCESS
      description: >-
        Involves glycoprotein biosynthesis without the lesion being specific to
        a named branch — the Other_Multiple_Glycosylation_Pathway_Disorders
        branch, whose members are there precisely because their lesion spans
        several. Ontology closure makes this subsume the two N-linked and the
        O-linked operands, which are kept so a member's own branch stays
        readable off the criterion that matched it.
      biological_processes:
      - preferred_term: protein glycosylation
        term:
          id: GO:0009101
          label: glycoprotein biosynthetic process
    - criterion_predicate: HAS_BIOLOGICAL_PROCESS
      description: >-
        Involves protein O-linked glycosylation — the
        Disorders_of_O-linked_Protein_Glycosylation branch (O-mannose,
        O-glucose/O-fucose, and the O-xylose glycosaminoglycan linker). Also
        satisfied by Other_Multiple_Glycosylation_Pathway_Disorders members
        whose branch-non-specific lesion reaches O-glycans.
      biological_processes:
      - preferred_term: protein O-linked glycosylation
        term:
          id: GO:0006493
          label: protein O-linked glycosylation
    - criterion_predicate: HAS_BIOLOGICAL_PROCESS
      description: >-
        Involves glycosaminoglycan biosynthesis — the GAG-*synthesis* arm that
        ICIMD places under O-linked protein glycosylation. Note this is
        biosynthesis, not the lysosomal catabolism of the mucopolysaccharidoses.
      biological_processes:
      - preferred_term: glycosaminoglycan biosynthetic process
        term:
          id: GO:0006024
          label: glycosaminoglycan biosynthetic process
    - criterion_predicate: HAS_BIOLOGICAL_PROCESS
      description: >-
        Involves ER protein folding — carried because
        Other_Multiple_Glycosylation_Pathway_Disorders requires it for UGGT1,
        whose lesion is re-glucosylation-based quality control of N-glycans.
      biological_processes:
      - preferred_term: protein folding in endoplasmic reticulum
        term:
          id: GO:0034975
          label: protein folding in endoplasmic reticulum
    - criterion_predicate: HAS_BIOLOGICAL_PROCESS
      description: >-
        Involves proteoglycan biosynthesis — carried because
        Disorders_of_O-linked_Protein_Glycosylation requires it for the two
        members that annotate only the proteoglycan-product classes
        (GO:0015012, GO:0050650) rather than the glycosaminoglycan class.
        Without it this disjunction was not in fact the union of its children's
        criteria, which is what the logic description above claims.
      biological_processes:
      - preferred_term: proteoglycan biosynthetic process
        term:
          id: GO:0030166
          label: proteoglycan biosynthetic process
    - criterion_predicate: HAS_BIOLOGICAL_PROCESS
      description: >-
        Involves protein deglycosylation — the
        Congenital_Disorders_of_Deglycosylation branch.
      biological_processes:
      - preferred_term: protein deglycosylation
        term:
          id: GO:0006517
          label: protein deglycosylation
    - criterion_predicate: HAS_BIOLOGICAL_PROCESS
      description: >-
        Involves oligosaccharide catabolism — the
        Congenital_Disorders_of_Deglycosylation branch (free-oligosaccharide
        trimming).
      biological_processes:
      - preferred_term: oligosaccharide catabolic process
        term:
          id: GO:0009313
          label: oligosaccharide catabolic process
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:33340416
    reference_title: "An international classification of inherited metabolic disorders (ICIMD)."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: >-
      The Congenital Disorders of Glycosylation (CDG) are divided into disorders
      affecting N-linked and O-linked protein glycosylation (including
      glycosaminoglycan synthesis), disorders of lipid glycosylation (including
      the disorders of glycosylphosphatidylinositol biosynthesis), and disorders
      with the potential to affect multiple glycosylation pathways (dolichol
      metabolism, Golgi transport and homeostasis, sialic acid metabolism, and
      others).
    explanation: >-
      The ICIMD category-18 subdivision this grouping's five nested children
      mirror. It is also what places the GPI-anchor disorders inside the
      glycosylation umbrella rather than beside it, which is the membership
      decision most likely to be questioned.
  - reference: PMID:33340416
    reference_title: "An international classification of inherited metabolic disorders (ICIMD)."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: >-
      they include disorders of glycan metabolism (including the congenital
      disorders of glycosylation but excluding disorders of glycogen metabolism)
    explanation: >-
      Sources the glycogen exclusion recorded in grouping_rationale: ICIMD keeps
      disorders of glycogen metabolism out of the glycan-metabolism categories,
      so Glycogen_Storage_Diseases is correctly not a child here.
- description: >-
    An entry assigned to ICIMD category 18 — congenital disorders of
    glycosylation, or any of its N-linked, O-linked, lipid, multiple-pathway, or
    other-glycan-metabolism subdivisions — via classifications.icimd_category
    belongs in this grouping.
  criteria_semantics: SUFFICIENT
  logic:
    operator: OR
    description: >-
      A discovery criterion, not an audit of the listed members: it is stated
      SUFFICIENT so that entries carrying an ICIMD category-18 value but not yet
      reached by any nested sub-grouping surface as candidate additions. Those
      currently outstanding are named in notes. It is deliberately not NECESSARY
      — most listed members carry no icimd_category value at all, and a
      NECESSARY reading would report that curation gap as a membership
      contradiction.
    operands:
    - criterion_predicate: HAS_CLASSIFICATION
      classification: "icimd_category:congenital_disorders_of_glycosylation"
      description: ICIMD category 18 at the category level.
    - criterion_predicate: HAS_CLASSIFICATION
      classification: "icimd_category:n_linked_protein_glycosylation"
      description: ICIMD 18, N-linked protein glycosylation.
    - criterion_predicate: HAS_CLASSIFICATION
      classification: "icimd_category:o_linked_protein_glycosylation"
      description: ICIMD 18, O-linked protein glycosylation (incl. GAG synthesis).
    - criterion_predicate: HAS_CLASSIFICATION
      classification: "icimd_category:lipid_glycosylation"
      description: ICIMD 18, lipid glycosylation (incl. GPI biosynthesis).
    - criterion_predicate: HAS_CLASSIFICATION
      classification: "icimd_category:multiple_glycosylation_pathways"
      description: >-
        ICIMD 18, disorders affecting multiple glycosylation pathways (dolichol
        metabolism, Golgi transport and homeostasis, sialic acid metabolism).
    - criterion_predicate: HAS_CLASSIFICATION
      classification: "icimd_category:other_glycan_metabolism"
      description: ICIMD 18, other disorders of glycan metabolism.
members:
- member: Congenital Disorders of Glycosylation
  member_type: GROUPING
  differentiating_mechanisms:
  - description: >-
      ICIMD 18, N-linked protein glycosylation. Defects in the assembly of the
      dolichol-linked oligosaccharide precursor, its transfer to nascent protein,
      or its Golgi remodeling, together with the nucleotide-sugar and dolichol
      supply lines feeding them (ALG1/3/9/12, DPM2, MPDU1, DOLK, PMM2, MPI, PGM1,
      MGAT2, SLC35A2, COG1, COG7, VPS51, DHRSX), plus ER glucosidase-I trimming
      (MOGS), terminal antenna galactosylation (B4GALT1), and Golgi V-ATPase
      assembly (CCDC115). The diagnostic readout is the
      serum transferrin glycoform profile, type I versus type II.
- member: Disorders of GPI Anchor Biosynthesis
  member_type: GROUPING
  differentiating_mechanisms:
  - description: >-
      ICIMD 18, lipid glycosylation. Defects in assembly, transfer, or
      post-attachment remodeling of the glycosylphosphatidylinositol anchor, so
      the affected clients are the GPI-anchored surface proteins rather than the
      N-glycoproteins (PIGA, PIGL, PIGP, PIGV, PIGO, PGAP2, PGAP3).
      Hyperphosphatasia
      from unanchored alkaline phosphatase, and — for the somatic PIGA case,
      paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria — complement-mediated hemolysis from
      lost CD55/CD59, are the distinguishing readouts.
- member: Disorders of O-linked Protein Glycosylation
  member_type: GROUPING
  differentiating_mechanisms:
  - description: >-
      ICIMD 18, O-linked protein glycosylation, including glycosaminoglycan
      synthesis. Defects in a glycan attached to a serine or threonine hydroxyl
      rather than an asparagine amide, divided by first sugar: O-mannose on
      alpha-dystroglycan (the dystroglycanopathy gene series), O-glucose on
      thrombospondin type-1 repeats (B3GLCT), and the O-xylose linker that starts
      every glycosaminoglycan chain (B3GAT3, EXTL3, EXT2). Distinguished from the
      N-glycan child by linkage chemistry and client protein family, and from the
      multiple-pathway child by the lesion being confined to this branch.
- member: Other Disorders of Multiple Glycosylation Pathways
  member_type: GROUPING
  differentiating_mechanisms:
  - description: >-
      ICIMD 18, disorders affecting multiple glycosylation pathways. Lesions
      upstream of, or lateral to, any single branch: UDP-sugar precursor supply
      serving glycosaminoglycan, glycolipid, and protein glycosylation at once
      (UGDH, UGP2), and ER re-glucosylation quality control of N-glycoproteins
      (UGGT1), and Golgi luminal conditions that disable several branches at
      once — pH via the V-ATPase a2 subunit (ATP6V0A2) and calcium handling
      (SLC10A7). Distinguished from the N-glycan child by the lesion not being
      specific to one glycosylation branch.
- member: Congenital Disorders of Deglycosylation
  member_type: GROUPING
  differentiating_mechanisms:
  - description: >-
      ICIMD 18, other disorders of glycan metabolism — the direction-reversed
      arm. Where the other three children fail to attach a glycan, these fail to
      remove and clear one: cytosolic peptide:N-glycanase (NGLY1) releasing the
      N-glycan from a retrotranslocated misfolded glycoprotein, and cytosolic
      alpha-mannosidase (MAN2C1) trimming the free oligosaccharide that release
      generates. The conforming module is cytosolic_deglycosylation, not
      congenital_disorder_of_glycosylation.
notes: >-
  Why the umbrella was created. The four children were already behaving as
  siblings without a parent: each one's grouping_rationale names the others as
  the home for what it excludes. Disorders_of_GPI_Anchor_Biosynthesis excludes
  DPM2-CDG and MPDU1-CDG because their Dol-P-Man lesion belongs "in the broader
  glycosylation grouping"; Congenital_Disorders_of_Glycosylation names GPI,
  multiple-pathway, and TSR O-fucosylation as sibling homes. That mutual
  cross-referencing was the signal that a node was missing, and it means the
  boundary work this grouping depends on was already done in prose.

  Resolved — the O-linked child. This grouping was created holding only four of
  ICIMD category 18's five subdivisions, with no member for O-linked protein
  glycosylation, and said so. Disorders of O-linked Protein Glycosylation now
  fills it, drawn from the five entries that already carried
  classifications.icimd_category o_linked_protein_glycosylation: the
  Dystroglycanopathy entry (O-mannose), Peters plus syndrome (O-glucose on
  thrombospondin type-1 repeats), and the three glycosaminoglycan-synthesis
  disorders ICIMD places in this subdivision rather than a separate one
  (B3GAT3, EXTL3, EXT2). All five evaluate SATISFIED against its NECESSARY
  criterion.

  Resolved — the candidate backlog. The eleven category-18 entries that belonged
  to no child are now placed, and the SUFFICIENT ICIMD criterion reports no
  candidates. Beyond the five O-linked entries above: MOGS-CDG, B4GALT1-CDG and
  CCDC115-CDG went to the N-glycan child, which is the same membership drift the
  2026-08-20 review corrected for seven other CDG entries; Developmental and
  Epileptic Encephalopathy 55 (PIGP) went to the GPI child; and Autosomal
  Recessive Cutis Laxa Type 2A (ATP6V0A2, Golgi pH) and Short Stature,
  Amelogenesis Imperfecta, and Skeletal Dysplasia with Scoliosis (SLC10A7, Golgi
  calcium) went to the multiple-pathway child. The last two annotate protein
  O-linked glycosylation and were deliberately *not* put in the O-linked child:
  their lesions are Golgi luminal conditions that disable several branches at
  once, and O-glycosylation being among a disorder's casualties does not make it
  an O-linked disorder.

  An empty candidate list is a statement about ICIMD coverage, not about
  completeness. It means every entry that *carries* a category-18 classification
  is now held by a child; entries whose glycosylation lesion is real but
  unclassified remain invisible to that criterion. Widening coverage of
  classifications.icimd_category across kb/disorders is the way to make the
  report say more.

  Resolved — UGP2. UGP2-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 83
  evaluated NOT_SATISFIED when this grouping was created, inheriting a
  pre-existing failure against its own child's NECESSARY criterion. The cause
  was a granularity mismatch in the criterion rather than a gap in the entry:
  ontology closure runs downward, so an entry annotated at an ancestor of the
  process a criterion names never satisfies it, and both criteria named only
  specific branches (GO:0006487, GO:0006493) while the entry annotated
  GO:0009100 glycoprotein metabolic process. The entry was right to decline a
  branch — its cited result is hypoglycosylated LAMP2, which the source does not
  resolve to N- or O-linked, and UGP2's lesion is UDP-glucose supply feeding
  several branches at once, which is why it sits in the multiple-pathway child
  at all.

  Fixed on both sides, each change standing on its own. The entry node moved to
  GO:0009101 glycoprotein biosynthetic process: more specific than what it
  carried, since it excludes the glycoprotein catabolism GO:0009100 also covers,
  and still branch-agnostic, so it claims no more than the source does. The
  child criterion and this disjunction each gained a GO:0009101 operand, which
  is the level the child's own rationale always described — grouping members "at
  the pathway-placement level" — and which closure makes subsume the named-branch
  operands, so nothing that satisfied them stops doing so. Note GO:0006486, the
  term an editor might reach for as "protein glycosylation", is **obsolete** —
  GO labels it "obsolete protein glycosylation" and records
  term_replaced_by GO:0009101, which is why GO:0009101 is both the replacement
  and the common ancestor of the N- and O-linked classes. An earlier version of
  this note said GO:0006486 did not exist; that came from passing the CURIE to
  an OLS *text* search, which matches nothing, and reading the empty result as
  absence. Resolve a CURIE by its term endpoint, not by searching for it.

  Resolved — MONDO closure, and it found a problem. The closure was declared
  UNKNOWN because the configured ols:mondo adapter cannot expand a class's
  descendants. Inverting the question removed the need to: instead of expanding
  MONDO:0015286 downward and testing members against the result, each member's
  own term is walked upward and the class looked up in its ancestor set. That is
  bounded per member, needs no 588 MB local build, and the OLS REST endpoint
  serves it directly. The result is in the mapping's consistency block: 24 of 38
  members descend from the mapped class, 14 do not, and the umbrella's concept
  therefore contains the MONDO class rather than equalling it. Whether the
  predicate should move from skos:exactMatch to skos:broadMatch is a live
  question with tooling consequences and is argued in that block rather than
  decided here.

  Coverage of the ICIMD category-18 classification itself is thin — 20 entries
  KB-wide, and only 20 of this grouping's 38 transitively held diseases carry a
  value (every one of those 20 KB-wide entries is now held here, which is why
  the SUFFICIENT criterion reports no candidates). That is why the ICIMD criterion is SUFFICIENT (a discovery lever) rather
  than NECESSARY (an audit of the listed members).
